<reason>Both sides argued well and stayed on the motion as written, with clean Q/A formatting. PRO built a strong intuitive frame (structural stake-chance-prize test, casino design toolkit, precautionary treatment of minors, and a memorable burden-reversal contrast between complaint-driven consumer law and licence-conditioned gambling law), and it effectively mined CON's protection package as a concession that the harm is real. But CON was more consistently on offense and did more comparative work. Two lines survived largely unanswered: (1) the definition drift — PRO's operative criterion moved from stake/chance/prize to friction/delivery to jackpot/tiers/near-miss, and CON's late blind-box example (rarity tiers, chase items, repeat buying to complete sets) went unaddressed in PRO's closing; and (2) the verification dilemma — PRO's own closing standard ("you may not take this transaction from a minor unless you can show you aren't") sits badly with PRO's actual mechanism of a platform "stated age," and CON's fork (either nothing changes, or full identity proof for every paying player, the cost PRO disclaimed) was never answered. Meanwhile CON neutralized PRO's best pressure question cleanly by making its protections universal defaults requiring no age sorting, and made a well-judged concession on tradeable-item/cash-out layers that cost it little while confining PRO's "money's worth" argument to a minority of games. PRO's raffle-car reply and publisher-set-value answer were good and kept the no-cash-out clash close, and the precautionary framing remained a real route. CON also carries an execution cost: two turns clipped for length, though the lost material was mostly a rehash or a sign-off line. Net: a clear but competitive CON win.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's handling of the age-verification exchange. PRO's Q1 tried to show CON's consumer package also needs to identify minors; CON answered that spend caps, plain-currency pricing, confirmations and refunds are universal defaults needing no age sorting, then forked PRO: a "stated age" checkbox is what gambling regulators exist to disbelieve, so PRO's gate is either cosmetic or imposes the identity checks PRO called excessive. PRO never answered that fork, and CON's closing crystallized it.</best_rebuttal>
